description: The Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) Dataset is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Nathan Sparks et al. Assessing tropical cyclone risk on a global scale given the infrequency of landfalling tropical cyclones (TC) and the short period of reliable observations remains a challenge. Synthetic tropical cyclone datasets can help overcome these problems. Here we present a new global dataset created by IRIS, the ImpeRIal college Storm model. Coverage: global; published in 2024. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
